A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Conformal changepoint localization. Their main text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable matching across moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original MNIST and SST-2 experiments, Gaussian simulations, empirical coverage estimates, and certified-data experiments in Section 6 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds HAR accelerometer and CIFAR-100 changepoint-localization experiments in Sections 6.3–6.4.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, p-value combination rules, and likelihood-ratio, KDE, and classifier score options remain unchanged. The added applications reuse CONCH; Section 5 revises its theoretical motivation rather than the reported localization procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds smartphone accelerometer activity changes from walking upstairs to standing, and CIFAR-100 color-image changes from bears to beavers. These substantially broaden empirical coverage beyond the retained MNIST, SST-2, and Gaussian settings.

E2.justification: Appendix A/Table 1 retains the same oracle, parametric learned, and KDE learned score comparisons. Newly discussed localization methods in Section 2 are not evaluated as baselines; the CIFAR classifier is a scoring component.

E3.justification: The added evaluations specify HAR with n=1000, changepoint 400, first-axis measurements, KDE scores, and Bonferroni combination; CIFAR uses n=800, changepoint 300, ResNet-18 scores, and minimum combination. Existing experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: The HAR case adds a limited diagnostic analysis: the reported mean difference is only -0.003 despite successful localization, accompanied by the raw signal and p-value plots. Earlier score comparisons, certified-data analyses, and exchangeability pre-testing analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains 1,000 trials and identical coverage uncertainty reporting. Appendix A also retains the same 1,000-simulation pre-testing assessments. The added applications introduce no new repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include a HAR 95% confidence set of size 24 with point estimate 403 for changepoint 400, and a CIFAR confidence interval [268, 329] with estimate 293 for changepoint 300. Existing MNIST, SST-2, Gaussian, and calibration results are unchanged. These are additional results under new settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Theorem 4.1 becomes v3 Theorem 3.1, dropping conditioning on nested data bags; Theorem C.1 and the coverage proof change accordingly. Section 5 generalizes the alternative to a change after any k, replaces Lebesgue-density assumptions with densities relative to Q+R, randomizes ties, and substantially revises the Neyman–Pearson proof. Its displayed p-value also reverses rank direction while retaining lower-tail rejection.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly adds accelerometer sequences to the claimed demonstrations. The central contributions remain single-changepoint localization, finite-sample confidence sets under exchangeability, and learned score functions motivated by a conformal Neyman–Pearson result.

C2.justification: v3 interprets HAR performance despite its small mean difference as evidence of usefulness beyond mean-focused localization. It also proposes using CONCH within an Isolate-Detect procedure for future multiple-changepoint work, elaborating v2's general extension suggestion.

D1.justification: The code reference changes from unspecified supplementary material to an explicit GitHub repository. v3 documents HAR bandwidth choices and the CIFAR pretrained model and source. Timing changes from experiments taking under 10 minutes to CONCH taking under 3 minutes per experiment; this wording does not establish a directly comparable speedup.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against sequential inference, nonparametric confidence intervals, and multiple-changepoint methods, adding works such as Saha and Ramdas, Cho and Kirch, Frick et al., and Verzelen et al. It removes the Bayesian/Fearnhead discussion and reverses the earlier characterization of whether Pettitt and Ross–Adams methods provide changepoint confidence sets.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes related-work paragraphs under more specific headings, adds an airplane-maintenance motivation, moves the coverage theorem from Section 4.2 to Section 3, and refines detection/localization terminology. Most remaining exposition and the appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 6–9 add substantial visual evidence: the HAR signal and localization plot, plus CIFAR image examples and localization plot. Earlier Gaussian and calibration figures are retained as Figures 10–12, and Table 1 is unchanged. New Figure 8 incorrectly labels the changepoint as 400 although its caption and experiment specify 300.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens empirical support, particularly through HAR's small mean difference, supplies a concrete code pointer, and narrows the coverage claim by removing conditioning unsupported by v2's argument. These provide useful net gains. However, the revised Section 5 p-value reverses rank direction without changing its rejection rule, and Figure 8 introduces conflicting changepoint labels, limiting the overall improvement.
